t.E938.agn: In their earlier evaluations, the SCF and JECFA had considered its use safe on the basis of these physico-chemical properties, without a toxicological evaluation. In 2024 EFSA re-evaluated argon and helium together, stated that as food additives they are of low toxicological concern and that their use does not raise a safety concern, and recommended adding CAS numbers to the EU specifications.
t.E938.found.0: In the EU, may be used in many foods at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E938.prod: A gas obtained by fractional distillation of liquefied air (physical separation).
t.E938.regx.0: Re-evaluated together with argon and helium; no safety concern, no ADI needed; adding a CAS number to the specification was recommended.
t.E938.regx.1: Group I additive; generally authorised at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E938.summary: A gas used to replace air in packaging or as a propellant. Prevents the product from oxidising or allows it to be dispensed from spray containers.
t.E938.what: A non-reactive packaging gas (argon) that replaces air in packaged foods. It is a chemically very stable noble gas.
